stem: The Periodic Table is arranged such that the properties of the elements show a number of trends.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A plot of the first ionisation energies for the first 18 elements is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain why the values show a general increase from atomic number 11 to 18.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Explain the decreases in first ionisation energies between

- atomic numbers 12 and 13,

- atomic numbers 15 and 16.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest an explanation for the trend in the first ionisation energies of the elements with atomic numbers 2, 10 and 18.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A plot of the melting points of the elements across the third period is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain the increase in melting point from atomic number 11 to 12.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest a reason why the increase from atomic number 12 to 13 is much smaller than the increase from atomic number 11 to 12.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State and explain the pattern of the melting points from atomic number 15 to 18.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Explain why the element with atomic number 14 has a melting point so much higher than the rest of the elements in the third period.
